symbols.name: Ncomp
symbols.role: neighborhood under the complement of the allowed-effect relation

symbols.name: Rk
symbols.role: best arbitrary difference-set rectangle mass at budget \(k\)

novel.justification: This strict validity margin is realistic whenever the nominal threshold does not coincide with one of the finitely many Hall coverage values; for fixed \(L\), its failure lies on a finite union of affine marginal surfaces.
This strict selector margin holds on each full-dimensional cell away from the finitely many feasibility and tie surfaces and is checkable from the identified marginal vectors.

definitions.name: Complement-relation neighborhood
definitions.construction: \(N_{S^{\mathsf c}}(A)=\{j\in X:\exists i\in A\text{ with }i-j\notin S\}\)

definitions.name: Cardinality--span--code selector
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{span}(S)=\max S-\min S,\quad\operatorname{code}(S)=\sum_{e\in S}2^{e+L-1},\quad S^\star=\min_{\prec}\mathcal V_{\mu,c}\), where \(\prec\) orders \((|S|,\operatorname{span}(S),\operatorname{code}(S))\) lexicographically.

definitions.name: Shortest valid interval
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_L=\{\{a,a+1,\ldots,b\}\subseteq E:a\leq b\},\qquad I^*=\min\{|I|:I\in\mathcal I_L,\ h_{\mu}(I)\geq c\}\)

definitions.name: Marginal interval concentration profiles
definitions.construction: \(Q_d(w)=\max_{0\leq a\leq L-w}\sum_{j=a}^{a+w-1}\mu_{d,j}\), for \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(1\leq w\leq L\).

definitions.name: Arbitrary and interval rectangle profiles
definitions.construction: \(B_k=\max_{1\leq a,b\leq L,\ a+b\leq k+1}\{Q_1(a)+Q_0(b)\},\qquad R_k=\max_{\varnothing\neq A,B\subseteq X,\ |A-B|\leq k}\{\mu_1(A)+\mu_0(B)\}\)

definitions.name: Confidence-robust certified family
definitions.construction:
\(\ell(S)=\min_{
u_1\in C_1,
u_0\in C_0}h_{(
u_0,
u_1)}(S),\qquad\widehat{\mathcal H}=\{S\subseteq E:\ell(S)\geq c\},\qquad\widehat S=\min_{\prec}\widehat{\mathcal H}\)

definitions.name: Min-cut and finite outer optimization
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Alg}\) evaluates \(h_{\mu}(S)\) by one source--row--column--sink minimum cut for each \(S\subseteq E\), and evaluates the outer optimum by enumerating \((A,B)\in\mathcal F_{\tau}\), deduplicating \(A-B\), and ordering the retained sets by \(\prec\).

definitions.name: Inverse Hall equality handle
definitions.construction: Use inverse equality analysis for \(|A-B|\geq|A|+|B|-1\) jointly with the active threshold-feasible Hall rectangles to characterize the marginal laws attaining the interval-price frontier.

statements.statement: For every \(S\subseteq E\), \[h_{\mu}(S)=\max_{A\subseteq X}\{\mu_1(A)-\mu_0(N_{S^{\mathsf c}}(A))\}=\max\!\left\{0,\max_{\substack{\varnothing\neq A,B\subseteq X\\A-B\subseteq S}}\bigl(\mu_1(A)+\mu_0(B)-1\bigr)\right\}.\] Both maxima and the minimum defining \(h_{\mu}(S)\) are attained, including when marginal cells are zero.
statements.justification: The identity converts robust coverage into finite Hall certificates with the correct complement orientation.
statements.gap: Koperberg2024 proves finite Strassen deficiency for a fixed relation; this specialization is supporting machinery and is not claimed as the headline novelty.
statements.consumer: The all-minimizer theorem and the confidence epigraph use the displayed Hall deficiencies as their certificates.

statements.statement: For every marginal pair, \[S\in\mathcal V_{\mu,c}\iff\exists(A,B)\in\mathcal F_{\tau}\text{ such that }A-B\subseteq S.\] Consequently, \[k^*=\min_{(A,B)\in\mathcal F_{\tau}}|A-B|,\qquad\mathcal K^*=\{A-B:(A,B)\in\mathcal F_{\tau},\ |A-B|=k^*\},\] where repeated difference sets are deduplicated. The inclusion-minimal valid sets are exactly the inclusion-minimal distinct members of \(\{A-B:(A,B)\in\mathcal F_{\tau}\}\), without positivity, strict Hall slack, or uniqueness assumptions.
statements.justification: This boundary-safe normal form replaces optimization over arbitrary unions of effect diagonals by high-mass marginal rectangles.
statements.gap: ZhangRichardson2025 treats intervals and single effect values, while Koperberg2024 fixes the allowed relation; neither characterizes every optimizer of the outer set problem.
statements.consumer: It reduces the seven-category remdesivir analysis to at most \((2^7-1)^2=16{,}129\) marginal rectangle candidates.

statements.statement: For every \(1\leq k\leq2L-1\), a valid effect set of cardinality at most \(k\) exists if and only if \(R_k\geq\tau\), and a valid interval of cardinality at most \(k\) exists if and only if \(B_k\geq\tau\). Therefore, \[k^*<I^*\iff\exists k\in\{1,\ldots,2L-1\}:B_k<\tau\leq R_k.\] This condition is also equivalent to every member of \(\mathcal K^*\), and hence \(S^\star\), being disconnected.
statements.justification: The profiles give an exact finite inequality frontier separating connected and disconnected robust optima.
statements.gap: Published ordinal bounds optimize scalar threshold events or intervals and do not compare sparse difference rectangles with marginal intervals.
statements.consumer: An analyst can diagnose whether interval reporting necessarily wastes effect categories before solving the complete outer problem.

statements.statement: Let \(L=3\). The deterministic selector \(S^\star\) is disconnected, equivalently every member of \(\mathcal K^*\) is disconnected, if and only if exactly one of \[d_2\geq c>b_2\qquad\text{or}\qquad1-\mu_{1,1}-\mu_{0,1}\geq c>b_3\] holds. In the first case \(k^*=2\) and \(\mathcal K^*\) is the deduplicated union of \[\bigl\{\{i-2,i\}:\mu_{1,i}+\mu_{0,0}+\mu_{0,2}-1\geq c,\ i\in X\bigr\}\] and \[\bigl\{\{-j,2-j\}:\mu_{0,j}+\mu_{1,0}+\mu_{1,2}-1\geq c,\ j\in X\bigr\}.\] In the second case \(k^*=3\) and \(\mathcal K^*=\{\{-2,0,2\}\}\). The strict and weak inequalities shown cover zero cells, exact coverage equalities, cardinality ties, span ties, and code ties.
statements.justification: Ternary outcomes are the first setting with genuine holes, and the theorem supplies the complete boundary-safe phase diagram.
statements.gap: ZhangRichardson2025 rules out the binary disconnected candidate, and LuDingDasgupta2018 bounds scalar ordinal events; neither gives this ternary selector partition.
statements.consumer: The result provides a transparent diagnostic for three-category clinical or educational endpoints and a proof template for larger supports.

statements.statement: For every \(L\geq3\), every \((\mu_0,\mu_1)\in\Delta_L^2\), and every \(0<\alpha<1\), the shortest arbitrary and interval-valid sets satisfy \[\frac{I^*}{k^*}\leq\frac{2L-1}{3},\qquad I^*-k^*\leq2L-4.\] For every fixed \(L\geq3\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), both constants are attained simultaneously by strictly positive symmetric marginals. Specifically, for any \(0<\varepsilon<\min\{\alpha/2,1-2\alpha\}\), the marginals with endpoint masses \((1-\varepsilon)/2\) and each interior mass \(\varepsilon/(L-2)\) have \(k^*=3\), attained by \(\{-L+1,0,L-1\}\), and \(I^*=2L-1\). Thus the interval-only oracle studied by ZhangRichardson2025 can be strictly larger by the displayed sharp factors than the arbitrary-set oracle.
statements.justification: The theorem quantifies exactly how much connected reporting can conceal in the coupling-robust causal problem.
statements.gap: ZhangRichardson2025 optimizes only intervals, while GaoShanSrinivasVijayaraghavan2025 compares structured sets under an observed response distribution; neither derives a sharp adversarial-coupling price.
statements.consumer: For the seven-category remdesivir endpoint, a valid three-effect set can coexist with the necessity of all thirteen effects under interval reporting.

statements.statement: The algorithm \(\mathsf{Alg}\) returns \(h_{\mu}(S)\), every member of \(\mathcal K^*\), and \(S^\star\) exactly. A fixed \(S\) requires a minimum cut on a network with \(2L+2\) vertices and \(L^2+2L\) capacitated arcs. The finite outer step examines at most \((2^L-1)^2\) nonempty pairs and at most \(2^{2L-1}\) effect sets; for \(L=7\), these counts are \(16{,}129\) and \(8{,}192\), respectively.
statements.justification: The theorem-level geometry is paired with an auditable exact computation for the motivating support size.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 gives generic polynomial programs, whereas this proposition exposes the problem-specific min-cut certificate and finite outer search.
statements.consumer: It makes the seven-category trial calculation reproducible without optimizing over latent joint tables separately for every candidate certificate.

statements.statement: For every \(n_0,n_1\geq1\) and \(0<\beta<1\), \[\inf_{\mu_0,\mu_1\in\Delta_L}\Pr\{\mu_0\in C_0,\ \mu_1\in C_1\}\geq1-\beta.\] Moreover, \(\ell(S)\) equals the finite linear program minimizing \(\sum_{i-j\in S}\gamma_{ij}\) over nonnegative \(\gamma\) whose row marginal lies in \(C_1\) and column marginal lies in \(C_0\). Hence \[\inf_{\mu_0,\mu_1\in\Delta_L}\Pr\{h_{\mu}(S)\geq c\text{ for every }S\in\widehat{\mathcal H}\}\geq1-\beta,\] even when the reported subfamily is selected from \(\widehat{\mathcal H}\).
statements.justification: A single simultaneous marginal event certifies all post-selected robust prediction sets without an additional multiplicity penalty.
statements.gap: MalloyTripathyNowak2021 covers multinomial parameters and HuangFangHanleyRosenblum2019 treats a scalar ordinal bound; neither certifies a selected family of common-coupling effect sets.
statements.consumer: Every reported set in a reanalysis of the Goldman trial receives an honest finite-sample certificate.

statements.statement: Fix \(\eta>0\). Uniformly over \((\mu_0,\mu_1)\in\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\), if both confidence radii do not exceed \(\eta/(4L)\), then \[\Pr(\widehat S\neq S^\star)\leq4L\exp\!\left\{-\frac{n_{\min}\eta^2}{8L^2}\right\}.\] Under stable allocation this bound converges to zero. The conclusion requires no unique Hall cut or separation among active rectangles.
statements.justification: The result separates honest coverage at boundaries from exact selector recovery on a transparent regular class.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019 analyzes directionally differentiable functionals and HuangFangHanleyRosenblum2019 a scalar optimizer; this theorem controls a discontinuous lexicographic set selector.
statements.consumer: Repeated randomized studies with a fixed ordinal endpoint recover the same population reporting set whenever the identified margins stay off feasibility boundaries.

statements.statement: Using the inverse Hall equality handle, characterize all \((\mu_0,\mu_1,\alpha)\) for which either \(I^*/k^*=(2L-1)/3\) or \(I^*-k^*=2L-4\), and determine whether simultaneous equality outside the symmetric endpoint-heavy family is possible when every marginal cell is positive.
statements.justification: An equality classification would turn the worst-case bound into a diagnostic theory of when interval reporting is maximally costly.
statements.gap: Neither the causal transport literature nor structured conformal prediction gives inverse equality conditions for a coupling-robust interval penalty.
statements.consumer: The classification would identify which marginal shapes warrant routine reporting of disconnected effect sets rather than intervals.

sampling_model.design: Two-arm randomized assignment identifies \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\); the cross-world coupling remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.units: Independent units with ordinal potential outcomes in \(X\), with arm sizes \(n_0\) and \(n_1\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary randomized treatment \(Z\in\{0,1\}\) with positive assignment probabilities.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Empirical multinomial marginals and simultaneous coordinatewise confidence polytopes \(C_0\) and \(C_1\); no cross-world dependence nuisance is estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sections 3 and 5 optimize coupling-robust prediction intervals, while Appendix D and Theorem 12 give sharp ordinal individual-effect probability-mass bounds.
The paper derives sharp Makarov-type bounds on the distribution function of the individual treatment effect and develops statistical inference for those bounds.
Proposition 6 gives Strassen's theorem with deficiency for a fixed finite relation.
The paper derives sharp bounds for the probabilities of benefit and strict benefit with ordinal outcomes.
The paper constructs pointwise-consistent confidence intervals for the partially identified fraction who benefit.
Theorem 1 characterizes minimum-average-volume level-set confidence regions for a multinomial parameter.
The standard bootstrap is consistent for a Gaussian directional limit if and only if the functional is fully differentiable.
The proposed dynamic program is approximately volume-optimal among unions of a fixed number of intervals under ordinary prediction coverage.
The paper computes sharp discrete causal bounds by polynomial programming.

tldr: Randomization identifies the two ordinal potential-outcome marginals but not their coupling. The proposal characterizes every shortest coupling-robust individual-effect set as a high-mass difference set, gives an exact boundary-safe ternary disconnectedness frontier, and proves that restricting reports to intervals has sharp multiplicative cost \((2L-1)/3\) and additive cost \(2L-4\). Exact min-cut computation and simultaneous multinomial confidence-polytopes provide finite-sample certification and uniform selector recovery away from explicit tie surfaces.

project_justification.gap: The closest ITE papers give sharp distributional bounds and optimize interval-valued reports, but no located result solves the outer cardinality optimization over arbitrary ordinal effect sets; Hall theory certifies a fixed support but does not solve that selection problem.
project_justification.niche: Ordinal outcomes create integer difference geometry in which disconnected sets can be dramatically shorter while remaining valid under every cross-world coupling.
project_justification.fill: The difference-set normal form, complete ternary frontier, sharp general-support interval price, and confidence-polytope inversion jointly deliver identification, geometry, computation, and honest reporting.

related_work: Zhang and Richardson (2025), Sections 3 and 5, study coupling-robust ITE prediction intervals; Appendix D and their Theorem 12 establish sharp ordinal individual-effect probability-mass bounds. The sharp interval-price theorem supplies a strict enlargement from their interval oracle to arbitrary effect sets, without attributing an explicit open problem to that paper. Fan and Park (2010) are the direct sharp distribution-of-ITE comparator: they derive Makarov-type distribution-function bounds and inference, whereas the present target selects a shortest common-coupling set of effect values and characterizes when that set is disconnected. Koperberg (2024) supplies finite Strassen--Hall deficiency for a fixed relation and is used only as identification machinery. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) derive sharp scalar ordinal benefit bounds through cumulative transportation arguments; the present target is a common-coupling multi-diagonal set. Gao, Shan, Srinivas, and Vijayaraghavan (2025) motivate measuring the exact price of geometric restrictions, but their structured conformal sets are evaluated under an observed outcome law rather than an adversarial potential-outcome coupling. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2021) motivate simplex confidence-region inversion, Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum (2019) address nonregular scalar ordinal-bound inference, and Fang and Santos (2019) explain why active-set ties require directional methods. Duarte and coauthors (2024) motivate exhaustive discrete computation but do not replace the symbolic frontier. Goldman and coauthors (2020) supply the seven-category randomized endpoint for the concrete application.
honest_scope: The Hall identity is established prior machinery specialized to this problem. The proposed novelty is the optimizer-wide difference-set geometry, exhaustive ternary frontier, and sharp interval price; all remain to be proved despite the completed finite checks. The confidence result is finite-sample honest but makes no efficiency claim. Selector recovery is asserted only on \(\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\); exact recovery on tie surfaces is not claimed. The irredundant general-\(L\) equality classification remains the open-ended question. When \(L=2\), the reduction agrees with Zhang and Richardson's result that the sole disconnected candidate cannot be shortest, providing the required binary sanity check.

seed_details.rebuttal: The hull bound depends on the additive-combinatorial constraint that every optimal set contains a threshold-feasible difference set; the cases of one, two, and at least three differences yield different sharp bounds, and strictly positive marginal laws are required for attainment.

seed_details.red_team: A cynical objection is that confidence-region projection makes validity automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: Validity is the easy half; the nontrivial requirements are an exact finite program that avoids an invalid robust min--max interchange and a uniform selector theorem with an explicit separation class.

seed_details.opportunity: Characterize every cardinality-minimal robust effect set as a threshold-feasible difference set, including simplex faces and binding Hall equalities.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Apply Strassen deficiency to the complement of the allowed-effect relation and identify the complement of each Hall neighborhood as the second side of a rectangle.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact fixed-support Hall theorem is occupied, but the optimizer-wide difference-set corollary is not stated in the searched ordinal ITE literature.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical objection is that this is an immediate corollary of finite Strassen deficiency.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection limits the result to a supporting lemma; it remains essential infrastructure but is not presented as the headline contribution.

seed_details.opportunity: Classify every marginal law attaining the sharp interval-price constants rather than merely construct one extremal family.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the extremal-instance construction by inverse additive combinatorics for equality in \(|A-B|\geq |A|+|B|-1\) together with equality in every Hall compression step.
seed_details.destination_search: No causal or structured-prediction source located characterizes equality under adversarial potential-outcome coupling.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical objection is that equality follows from standard inverse sumset theory.
seed_details.rebuttal: Inverse sumset structure controls only support geometry; the marginal mass inequalities and robust-coupling feasibility add independent equality restrictions.

seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the exact marginal surfaces on which uniform recovery of the deterministic shortest-set selector is impossible.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Move from directional differentiability of a real-valued maximum to local asymptotic indistinguishability of two categorical laws whose discrete selectors differ.
seed_details.destination_search: The searched nonregular-inference sources establish bootstrap failure or scalar-bound inference, not an exact impossibility region for this selector.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical objection is that discontinuity trivially rules out uniform consistency.
seed_details.rebuttal: Discontinuity alone does not identify the maximal regular region or yield the two-point lower bound at each feasibility and tie-break surface.

seed_details.opportunity: Derive the sharp robust-coupling price of restricting the effect set to a union of at most \(r\) intervals for every \(r\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace one-interval hull compression by an \(r\)-component covering theorem for integer difference sets.
seed_details.destination_search: Structured conformal work optimizes unions of intervals under an observed response law, not under the infimum over fixed-marginal couplings.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical objection is that the result is a routine interpolation between arbitrary sets and intervals.
seed_details.rebuttal: The number of connected components of a difference set is controlled by additive structure rather than cardinality alone, so no routine interpolation was found; feasibility is nevertheless too uncertain for the first version.

seed_details.opportunity: Construct shortest disconnected prediction sets conditional on covariates with uniform coupling-robust coverage.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The finite marginal vectors become nuisance functions of covariates, so every Hall mass inequality must be estimated uniformly before discrete selection.
seed_details.destination_search: Conditional Makarov inference is adjacent, but the exact target requires a separate function-class and smoothing theory not supplied by the present fixed-support substrate.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical objection is that this merely applies the population theorem pointwise in covariates.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform estimation and selection across covariates are not pointwise corollaries, but the needed smoothness layer would obscure the sharper fixed-margin structural result.
